resale_co.name: Certificate of Occupancy / Certificate of Continued Use (combined certificate of smoke alarm, carbon monoxide alarm and compliance, CSDCMAC)
resale_co.issued_by: Borough of Eatontown inspector (Housing Official, Code Enforcement Officer, Fire Marshal or Fire Inspector)
resale_co.lead_time: Fees rise when the request is made 10 or fewer business days before the change of occupancy. All fees are paid with the application before any inspection.
resale_co.valid_for: 60 days (Code §116-6B); the code also says CSDCMAC inspections are valid for six months
requirements: Inspection for fitness for habitation under Borough Code §116-8 before the home is sold
Any outstanding permit issues must be closed; Zoning Officer certifies compliance
Smoke detectors on each level and within 10 feet of sleeping quarters, working and under 10 years old; 10-year sealed battery units; AC powered units cannot be swapped for battery units
Carbon monoxide detectors within 10 feet of sleeping quarters, working, under 7 years old (standalone) or 10 years (combination)
Monitored fire alarm systems must be made available for testing, with a certificate of inspection

Checklist items include working doors and keyless deadbolts, GFCI in bathrooms, covered electrical boxes and plates, 4-inch house numbers, handrails on stairs over four risers, unbroken operable windows, safe sidewalk/driveway/apron/foundation, heating system and flue, water heater overflow pipe, metal dryer vent, minimum 60 amp service, sump pump on a dedicated receptacle
Application states the future owner's name and address and who will allow entry
All utilities (gas, electric, water) must be on at the time of the inspection (2026 Housing checklist)

fees.label: Certificate of occupancy and inspection (combined with smoke/CO certificate), one and two family, more than 10 business days before the change of occupancy
fees.quote: More than 10 business days prior to the change of occupancy: $100.

fees.label: One and two family, 4 to 10 business days before
fees.quote: Four to 10 business days prior to the change of occupancy: $135.

fees.label: One and two family, fewer than 4 business days before
fees.quote: Fewer than four business days prior to the change of occupancy: $200.

fees.label: Transfer of residential properties (lawful two-family homes charged separately)
fees.quote: $200 for transfer of residential properties (lawful two-family homes charged separately).

fees.label: Buyer backs out and a new buyer purchases before occupancy (updated application)
fees.quote: A $35 fee if a tenant/buyer backs out of lease/purchase prior to occupancy

resale_co.how_to_apply: Apply online for a Resale inspection through the Borough's SDL Portal (https://www.sdlportal.com/towns/nj/monmouth/eatontown/requests/certificate; an account is needed), then pay online with the link on the Borough's 'Apply for a CO - Housing' sheet, or drop off a check at the Housing office on the 2nd floor of Borough Hall, 47 Broad Street. Fees are paid with the application before any inspection. The sheet and the 2026 Housing checklist are on the Borough's Applications & Forms page (Housing section). Questions: 732-860-5513 or ayates@eatontownnj.com.
resale_co.contact_title: Housing Department contact named on the CO application sheet (listed as Technical Assistant / Administrative Assistant on Borough pages)

evidence.quote: Eatontown Borough shall perform inspections in accordance with the New Jersey Uniform Fire Code before any one- and two-family or attached single-family structure is sold, leased, or otherwise made subject to a change of occupancy for residential purposes.
A certificate of occupancy/continued use will be valid for 60 days. If after 60 days a tenant/buyer has not occupied the property, then a new certificate must be applied for.
All fees shall be paid upon application before any inspection may be conducted and the issuance of a certificate of occupancy.
Applicants shall satisfy that the structure meets all code requirements, and any outstanding permit issues must be closed.
Nicholas Cosentino Housing Officer
John Bowen Housing Officer
Note: Please do not schedule any closings prior to final building inspections.
Please click the link below to apply for a Resale, rental, or Multiple Dwelling Inspection.
You can also drop off a check to the Housing office, located on the 2nd floor of the Borough Hall.
If you have any questions, please feel free to contact our office at 732-860-5513 or ayates@eatontownnj.com
All utilities (gas, electric, water) must be operational at the time of the inspection.

resale_co.notes: Re-checked 2026-10-27. The Borough's Applications & Forms page now has a Housing section with an 'Apply for a CO - Housing' sheet (PDF modified October 22, 2026) and an 'Eatontown Housing Checklist 2026'. The sheet sends applicants to the SDL Portal for a Resale, rental or Multiple Dwelling Inspection (the portal needs a login, so its form and fee screen could not be read), then to an online payment link, or a check can be dropped off at the Housing office. It lists the Housing Department at (732) 860-5513 and ayates@eatontownnj.com; the 2026 checklist header lists (732) 389-7616. The checklist covers one/two family sales and rentals and requires utilities on at inspection; peeling paint, plumbing, appliances, screens and lead paint items are marked rentals only. The Building / Construction page still lists Housing Officers Nicholas Cosentino and John Bowen (housing@eatontownnj.com link), and asks that no closings be scheduled before final building inspections. The 'Thinking of Selling Your House?' page still says 'Coming soon!'. Chapter 116 (Ord. No. 17-2026, adopted August 26, 2026) could not be re-read this time (ecode360 blocked); the quotes are from the full print-view read on 2026-10-13. It combines the town habitability inspection and the state smoke/CO certificate into one certificate. The fee section lists both a timing-based one and two family schedule ($100 / $135 / $200) and a flat '$200 for transfer of residential properties (lawful two-family homes charged separately)'; it is unclear which applies to a sale, so confirm with the Housing Division. The code also gives two validity periods (60 days in §116-6B and six months for CSDCMAC inspections in §116-6A). Fire extinguishers and lead-based paint certifications are listed for rentals only.

requirements: Smoke detectors on each level and within 10 feet of sleeping quarters, working and less than 10 years old
10-year sealed battery single station smoke alarms (ANSI/UL 217); AC powered alarms from original construction or rehabilitation stay AC powered
Carbon monoxide detectors within 10 feet of sleeping quarters, working, under 7 years old (standalone) or 10 years (combination)
No fire extinguisher for owner sales; the code lists extinguishers for rental and apartment units only

authorities.how_to_apply: The smoke/CO certificate is not applied for separately: Eatontown issues one combined certificate after its Housing inspection, applied for through the SDL Portal (see resale certificate). The Bureau of Fire Safety page points to the Applications & Forms page to obtain a Local Certificate of Occupancy.
authorities.contact_title: Fire Marshal (also listed as Chief Code Enforcement Officer)

evidence.quote: To protect the health, safety, and wellness of all residents and first responders, the owner shall obtain a combined certificate of smoke alarm, carbon monoxide alarm, and compliance.

The certificate of smoke alarm, carbon monoxide alarm and compliance (CSDCMAC) inspections are designed to efficiently accomplish this purpose and are valid for a six-month period from the date issued.
Fire extinguishers shall be installed in all rental and apartment units with a minimum rating of 2A-10B:C

To apply for a fire permit, register a new business with the Fire Prevention Bureau, or obtain a Local Certificate of Occupancy, please visit our Applications and Forms page located on the Borough homepage to access the required forms, documentation, and application information.

fire_cert.notes: The state fire directory lists the Eatontown Housing office (47 Broad St, (732) 389-7615) as the smoke detector compliance office, with Fire Marshal Patrick Renaldi as fire official. Under the August 2026 ordinance the smoke/CO certificate is issued together with the certificate of occupancy, so the fees shown are the same combined fees. The Fire Prevention Bureau page cited before (/departments/fire-prevention-bureau) is gone (404); the Borough's current page is /departments/bureau-of-fire-safety. It lists Fire Marshal Patrick Renaldi ((732) 720-2582, prenaldi@eatontownnj.com), Administrative Assistant Ashley Yates ((732) 389-7615, ayates@eatontownnj.com), inspectors Todd Feiter and Brian Pericone, and the bureau contact fireprev@EatontownNJ.com, (732) 389-7620. The Land Use, Zoning & Code Enforcement page lists Patrick Renaldi as Chief Code Enforcement Officer.

other_items.label: Open permits and zoning
other_items.detail: Outstanding permit issues must be closed and the Zoning Officer must certify compliance before the certificate is issued. The Building / Construction page also asks that no closings be scheduled before final building inspections on open permits.
